headline: NEW to scans (Fri Oct 24, Istanbul) -- Eight foreign ministers condemn Ansar Allah escalation in joint statement
dek: Foreign ministers from eight nations gathered in Istanbul (first meeting of its kind, hosted by Fidan) and jointly condemned 'in the strongest terms the unacceptable escalation by the Ansar Allah militia', including strikes on Saudi civilians/civilian infrastructure and attacks on commercial shipping…
sources: Turkish Defence Minister Yasar Guler (Friday remarks); Saudi Foreign Ministry statement (Faisal bin Farhan + Ishaq Dar bilateral); joint statement of the Istanbul ministerial (UK, France, Germany, Italy + R4: Pakistan, S
fault_line: Is the Makkah pact a real collective-defence commitment, or a deterrence signal that stops at the Ansar Allah question because Article 2 was written for states, not militias?

sections.what_happened: Foreign ministers from eight nations gathered in Istanbul (first meeting of its kind, hosted by Fidan) and jointly condemned 'in the strongest terms the unacceptable escalation by the Ansar Allah militia', including strikes on Saudi civilians/civilian infrastructure and attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, calling on the Ansar Allah to cease all military actions and return to the political process. Separately, Guler said Turkiye does not expect its troops to engage in combat with the Ansar Allah under the Makkah defence pact: 'The main purpose of our possible military support to Saudi Arabia will be to strengthen deterrence. We absolutely do not foresee entering into any conflict with the Ansar Allah.' The pact (signed August, submitted to Turkey's parliament this week; Saudi Arabia and Pakistan have ratified) says an attack on one member is an attack on all, but Article 2 covers attack by 'another country or a group of countries' -- leaving its application to non-state Ansar Allah strikes unclear.
sections.what_verified: The National (T2) reporting, carrying the Saudi Foreign Ministry statement (T1, STATE SA) and Guler's own remarks (T1, STATE TR). The ministers' statements are primary for their own positions.
sections.what_disputed: The joint statement's condemnation does not create an enforcement mechanism: Guler's own caveat (deterrence only, no combat foreseen) and the Article 2 non-state-actor gap both limit what the pact commits Turkiye to. Pakistan's ratification was already recorded (totw-20261024-1800-02 Makkah pact item); this record adds the Istanbul joint statement + Guler combat caveat, not the pact itself.
sections.why_matters: The gap IS the story: eight ministers condemn, one defence minister immediately draws the line -- deterrence yes, combat no. Pair Guler's quote with the Article 2 wording and the ratification count (2 of 3) to show why the pact may not mean what its 'attack on one is attack on all' headline suggests.
